parole.significato: A strong unpasteurised soft cheese from Asturias, Spain, made from cow milk.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Asturian afuega'l pitu. Literally "choke the chicken". According to local legend, the cheese is deemed to be ready when it is strong enough to choke a chicken that eats it.

parole.significato: A dish from Asturias, consisting of a bread roll with a piece of chorizo inside.
A dish from Asturias, made of white beans, pork products, chorizo and various other ingredients.
A dish from Asturias, made of white beans and clams.
parole.testo: From Asturian fabes con amasueles (“beans with clams”).

parole.significato: a dialect of Western Asturian-Leonese spoken in the upper half of the Sil valley and El Bierzo
parole.testo: Borrowed from Asturian paḷḷuezu, from palloza (“hut with thatched roof made of straw”), as this dialect was spoken in mountain villages of northwestern León and adjacent Asturias and became known as the "language of pallozas."

parole.significato: An endangered breed of sheep indigenous to the Asturias province of Northern Spain.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Asturian xaldu ("inhabitant of the valleys").
